full_text_en:
Zhang Qi — Financial Instrument Fraud Case

Promulgated by the Supreme People’s Court (2001) No. 1

Criminal Judgment of the Supreme People's Court of the People's Republic of China

(1999) Xing Fu Zi No. 103

Defendant: Zhang Qi (alias Zhang Mingliang), male, born on November 14, 1956, Han Chinese, native of Beijing, unemployed (from June 1995 to 1996 employed as Manager of the Investment Promotion Department of Beijing Yindun Police Industry & Trade Group), residing at No. 7, Gaoliangqiao East Lane, Xicheng District, Beijing. Arrested on October 7, 1997. Currently in custody.

The Beijing No. 1 Intermediate People's Court, upon hearing the case initiated by the former Branch of the Beijing People's Procuratorate charging the defendant Zhang Qi with financial instrument fraud, rendered a criminal judgment (1998) Yi Zhong Xing Chu Zi No. 1162 on September 10, 1998, finding the defendant Zhang Qi guilty of financial instrument fraud, sentencing him to death, deprivation of political rights for life, and confiscation of all personal property. After the judgment, Zhang Qi refused to accept the verdict and appealed. The Beijing High People's Court, by criminal judgment (1998) Gao Xing Zhong Zi No. 599 on March 18, 1999, dismissed the appeal, affirmed the original judgment, and submitted the case to this Court for approval in accordance with the law. This Court lawfully formed a collegiate panel and conducted a review of the case. The review is now concluded.

Upon review, it is ascertained that:

In June 1996, Zhang Hongfa (separately prosecuted), Vice Director of the Liaison Center of the Basic Theory of Public Security Committee of the China Police Academy and concurrently Vice President of Beijing Yindun Police Industry & Trade Group (hereinafter referred to as "Beijing Yindun Group"), together with the defendant Zhang Qi, who was then serving as Manager of the Investment Promotion Department of Beijing Yindun Group, conspired to defraud bank deposits of depositors by offering high interest as an inducement. Through Gao Jianzhong and Mou Yijie (both separately prosecuted), they learned that the Beijing Department Store (later renamed Beijing Wangfujing Department Store (Group) Co., Ltd.) had idle funds. They instructed Gao Jianzhong and Mou Yijie to deceive the Beijing Department Store, claiming that if the store deposited its funds with the West Chang'an Street Office of CITIC Industrial Bank, in addition to the interest paid by the bank as prescribed by the state, the borrower would also pay a portion of interest higher than the bank rate after the funds were lent out. On July 5, 1996, the Beijing Department Store deposited RMB 20 million with the West Chang'an Street Office of CITIC Industrial Bank. Subsequently, Zhang Hongfa and Zhang Qi instructed Gao Jianzhong and Mou Yijie to use the photocopy of the reserved seal card of the Beijing Department Store provided by Chen Tong (separately prosecuted), an employee of the West Chang'an Street Office of CITIC Industrial Bank, to privately engrave a "Beijing Department Store Financial Seal" and the seal of Liu Yulan, the chief accountant of the store. Zhang Hongfa forged a bank remittance voucher for the transfer of funds by the Beijing Department Store. On July 10, using the forged bank remittance voucher, Zhang Hongfa went to the West Chang'an Street Office of CITIC Industrial Bank and transferred RMB 20 million into the account of the Liaison Center of the Basic Theory of Public Security Committee of the China Police Academy held at the same office, thereby defrauding the Beijing Department Store of its deposit of RMB 20 million. After the incident, Zhang Qi received RMB 80,000 of the illicit proceeds; the rest was used by Zhang Hongfa and Beijing Yindun Group, causing losses of over RMB 12 million.

In March 1997, Tian Jidao (at large), the legal representative of Beijing Kaibo Te Investment Consulting Co., Ltd., asked Zhang Qi to help raise funds. Zhang Qi, through Guan Sihu (at large), Li Qiliang (separately prosecuted), and others, used the aforementioned methods to induce China Commodity Inspection Newspaper Agency to deposit RMB 10 million with the Chongwenmen Sub-Branch of Bank of China Beijing Branch on March 27 of the same year. Thereafter, Tian Jidao arranged for others to privately engrave the financial seal and the legal representative's seal of China Commodity Inspection Newspaper Agency, had Zhang Qi compare them, and then forged a bank remittance voucher for the transfer of RMB 9.9 million from China Commodity Inspection Newspaper Agency to Beijing Kaibo Te Investment Consulting Co., Ltd. On March 31, 1997, Zhang Qi instructed Li Qiliang to go to the Chongwenmen Sub-Branch of Bank of China Beijing Branch to transfer RMB 9.9 million into the account of Beijing Kaibo Te Investment Consulting Co., Ltd. held at the Lianhuahe Sub-Branch of Bank of China Beijing Branch, thereby defrauding China Commodity Inspection Newspaper Agency of its deposit of RMB 9.9 million. After the incident, Zhang Qi received RMB 160,000 of the illicit proceeds; the rest was used by Beijing Kaibo Te Investment Consulting Co., Ltd. After the case was uncovered, a total of approximately RMB 2.3 million in illicit proceeds and goods were recovered; over RMB 7.5 million remained unrecovered.

Between May and June 1997, Zhang Qi became acquainted with Zu Feng (at large), Vice General Manager of Beijing Gongda Real Estate Company. Zu Feng learned that Beijing Huachuan Economic Trade Development Company had RMB 6 million in idle funds and intended to deposit them with a bank to earn high interest. He then conspired with Zhang Qi and Tie Qi (separately prosecuted) to defraud this sum. On July 31, 1997, Zu Feng, through others, used the aforementioned methods to induce Beijing Huachuan Economic Trade Development Company to deposit RMB 6 million with the Xuanwumen Sub-Branch of Bank of China Beijing Branch. Subsequently, Zu Feng obtained a photocopy of the reserved seal card and deposit slip of Beijing Huachuan Economic Trade Development Company and handed them to Tie Qi. Tie Qi instructed Wang Yanqiu (co-defendant in the same case, already sentenced) to use the reserved seal card to privately engrave a "Beijing Huachuan Economic Trade Development Company Financial Seal" and the seal of Bao Hongxi, the legal representative of the company. Zhang Qi compared the privately engraved seals and then forged a bank remittance voucher for the transfer of RMB 5.9 million from Beijing Huachuan Economic Trade Development Company to Beijing Gongda Real Estate Company. On August 4, 1997, Tie Qi and others, using the forged bank remittance voucher, went to the Xuanwumen Sub-Branch of Bank of China Beijing Branch and transferred RMB 5.9 million into the account of Beijing Gongda Real Estate Company, thereby defrauding Beijing Huachuan Economic Trade Development Company of its deposit of RMB 5.9 million. After the incident, Zhang Qi received RMB 50,000 of the illicit proceeds; the rest was used by Beijing Gongda Real Estate Company. After the case was uncovered, over RMB 5.19 million in illicit proceeds were recovered; over RMB 700,000 remained unrecovered.

In August 1997, Zu Feng learned that Beijing Transmission and Substation Company had RMB 10 million in idle funds. He then conspired with Zhang Qi and Tie Qi to defraud this sum. On August 6, 1997, Zu Feng induced Beijing Transmission and Substation Company to deposit RMB 10 million with the Lianhuahe Sub-Branch of Bank of China Beijing Branch using the aforementioned methods. On the following day, Zu Feng obtained a photocopy of the reserved seal card and deposit slip of Beijing Transmission and Substation Company from its depositor and handed them to Tie Qi. Tie Qi had Wang Yanqiu use the reserved seal card to privately engrave a "Beijing Transmission and Substation Company Financial Seal" and the seal of Cao Jinen, the legal representative of the company. Zhang Qi compared the privately engraved seals and then forged a bank remittance voucher for the transfer of RMB 9.8 million from Beijing Transmission and Substation Company to Beijing Gongda Real Estate Company. On August 11, 1997, when Tie Qi instructed another person to go to the Lianhuahe Sub-Branch of Bank of China Beijing Branch to make the transfer, bank staff discovered that the seal on the bank remittance voucher did not match the reserved seal, and the fraud attempt failed.

In summary, the defendant Zhang Qi, acting in concert with others, used forged bank remittance vouchers on four occasions to defraud depositors of a total of RMB 45.6 million (of which RMB 9.8 million was an attempted fraud), and Zhang Qi received RMB 290,000 of the illicit proceeds. After the case was uncovered, over RMB 15.1 million in illicit proceeds and goods were recovered; over RMB 20 million remained unrecovered.

The above facts are confirmed by the seized forged seals and bank remittance vouchers, expert conclusions, witness testimony, and the confessions of co-defendants, as well as the admissions of the defendant Zhang Qi. They are sufficient to establish the truth.

Opinion of the Court:

The defendant Zhang Qi, acting in concert with others, used forged bank remittance vouchers to defraud depositors of their deposits. His conduct constitutes the crime of financial instrument fraud. The amount involved in the fraud was exceptionally large, causing particularly significant losses to the interests of the State. In the joint crime, Zhang Qi participated in the conspiracy, compared the forged seals, forged the bank remittance vouchers, instructed others to effectuate the transfers, and shared in the illicit proceeds, playing a principal role; he is thus a principal offender. However, considering that Zhang Qi assisted others in committing the financial instrument fraud, that the vast majority of the illicit proceeds were possessed by others or other entities, that the amount of illicit proceeds Zhang Qi personally received was not substantial, that his attitude toward admitting guilt was relatively good, and that his role in the joint crime was comparatively minor relative to that of Zhang Hongfa and others, the imposition of the death sentence on him need not be carried out immediately. The facts found in the first-instance and second-instance judgments are clear, the evidence is reliable and sufficient, and the conviction is accurate. The trial procedures were lawful. However, the sentence was inappropriate.

Pursuant to Article 199 of the Criminal Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, Article 285(3) of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Implementation of the Criminal Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, and Article 12(1), Article 194(2), Article 199, Article 26(1) and (4), Article 48(1), Article 57(1), and Article 59 of the Criminal Law of the People's Republic of China, the judgment is as follows:

1. The sentencing portion of the criminal judgment (1998) Gao Xing Zhong Zi No. 599 of the Beijing High People's Court and the criminal judgment (1998) Yi Zhong Xing Chu Zi No. 1162 of the Beijing No. 1 Intermediate People's Court concerning the defendant Zhang Qi is hereby set aside;

2. The defendant Zhang Qi is convicted of financial instrument fraud and sentenced to death, with a two-year reprieve, deprivation of political rights for life, and confiscation of all personal property.

This judgment shall become legally effective upon service.

Presiding Judge: Gao Guijun
Judge: Wang Guixiao
Acting Judge: Liu Hongzhang

December 7, 2000
